title: Speedy's memorial service
summary: Jones describes the memorial for his wife Violet Speedy, with Sarah singing and lighting by Carl Carruthers.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: You know, Jimmy, we have made references back and forth during these tapes to Speedy, but we haven't really talked about her. Speedy, your wife, Violet Jones.
Yes.
She had a career in show business too, right?
Uh-huh.
She was a dancer, is that right?
Yeah.
And you said an actress.
Yes, she was a good actress.
What all did she do?
All right. She worked with Lena Horne, you know.
When, at what point?
Oh, was it the Cotton Club? You know, one of those things. Gee, I gave Marl all those notes. Because Marl Young and Rozelle Gayle served at her service, you know?
Uh-huh.
And well she had a, it was a memorial, really. Because she was a swinger.
Yeah. Uh-huh.
So I just kept her image going, you know. And Sarah sang. Jerome played. Rozelle played organ. And John Collins played.
Uh-huh.
We didn't play any hymns or anything. No, nothing like that, you know.
Uh-huh.

We even had the lighting set up. You know, because Carl Carruthers, who used to do the lights for Sammy Davis, Jr. and Count Basie, went there early and had pin, red and white lights. He set the whole thing up, you know.
Uh-huh.
And I just had a great big picture of her there, you know. And when we told people don't send flowers, send contributions to the Cancer Fund.
Uh-huh.
And we got a lot -- we got some great results out of that, you know.
That's good.
But she was quite a lady. She was the best friend I had outside of my parents. Because I'd gone through some illnesses and she helped to keep me on my feet.
